## RemediationPolicy

RemediationPolicy says which actions are allowed, on which targets, within which bounds, and whether a human
must approve. Its generation is part of every plan digest, so changing it invalidates pending approvals.
The name must be a DNS label (at most 63 characters), since requests reference it.

- API version: `remediation.shadewright.io/v1alpha1`
- Kind: `RemediationPolicy`
- Scope: Cluster

Validation rules:

- name must be at most 63 characters: `size(self.metadata.name) <= 63`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata` | [ObjectMeta](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#objectmeta-v1-meta) | No | Standard object metadata. |
| `spec` | [RemediationPolicySpec](#remediationpolicyspec) | Yes | spec is the policy. |
| `status` | [RemediationPolicyStatus](#remediationpolicystatus) | No | status reports whether the policy is usable. |

## RemediationRequest

RemediationRequest is one proposed fix: a typed action on one object, carried out as a GitOps pull request
after deterministic policy allows it.

- API version: `remediation.shadewright.io/v1alpha1`
- Kind: `RemediationRequest`
- Scope: Namespaced

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata` | [ObjectMeta](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#objectmeta-v1-meta) | No | Standard object metadata. |
| `spec` | [RemediationRequestSpec](#remediationrequestspec) | Yes | spec is the plan.<br>Rule: spec is immutable; a changed plan is a new RemediationRequest<br>Rule: AdjustKedaMaxReplicas can only target a keda.sh ScaledObject<br>Rule: SetContainerMemoryLimit can only target an apps/v1 Deployment or StatefulSet |
| `status` | [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus) | No | status is the progress, written by the controller. |

### Action

- setContainerMemoryLimit must be set if and only if type is SetContainerMemoryLimit: `self.type == 'SetContainerMemoryLimit' ? has(self.setContainerMemoryLimit) : !has(self.setContainerMemoryLimit)`

Used by: [RemediationRequestSpec](#remediationrequestspec).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | [ActionType](#actiontype) | Yes | type selects the action.<br>One of `AdjustKedaMaxReplicas`, `SetContainerMemoryLimit` |
| `adjustKedaMaxReplicas` | [AdjustKedaMaxReplicas](#adjustkedamaxreplicas) | No | adjustKedaMaxReplicas holds the parameters for AdjustKedaMaxReplicas.<br>Rule: desiredValue must differ from previousValue |
| `setContainerMemoryLimit` | [SetContainerMemoryLimit](#setcontainermemorylimit) | No | setContainerMemoryLimit holds the parameters for SetContainerMemoryLimit.<br>Rule: desired must differ from previous<br>Rule: previous and desired must be whole bytes<br>Rule: previous must be between 1Mi and 1Ti<br>Rule: desired must be between 1Mi and 1Ti |

### ActionType

ActionType is the closed catalog of remediation actions (ADR-0003). Adding a value needs typed parameters,
policy bounds, a GitOps patcher and a test that it is refused outside its bounds.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `AdjustKedaMaxReplicas`, `SetContainerMemoryLimit`

Used by: [Action](#action), [PolicyAction](#policyaction).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `AdjustKedaMaxReplicas` | ActionAdjustKedaMaxReplicas changes maxReplicaCount of a KEDA ScaledObject. |
| `SetContainerMemoryLimit` | ActionSetContainerMemoryLimit changes the memory limit of one container in a workload's pod template. |

### AdjustKedaMaxReplicas

AdjustKedaMaxReplicas changes spec.maxReplicaCount of a ScaledObject. previousValue must match the file in
Git when the patch is applied, or the plan is stale.


Validation rules:

- desiredValue must differ from previousValue: `self.desiredValue != self.previousValue`

Used by: [Action](#action).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `previousValue` | integer | Yes | previousValue is the value the plan was made against.<br>Maximum: 1000<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `desiredValue` | integer | Yes | desiredValue is the new maxReplicaCount.<br>Maximum: 1000<br>Minimum: 1 |

### AzureKeyVaultKey

AzureKeyVaultKey is a key in Azure Key Vault that may only sign (ADR-0006).


Used by: [Signer](#signer).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keyID` | string | Yes | keyID is the key identifier, with or without a version, for example https://&lt;vault>.vault.azure.net/keys/github-app. It follows the Key Vault naming rules, as the signer does: a vault name of 3 to 24 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens that starts with a letter, ends with a letter or digit and has no consecutive hyphens; a key name of 1 to 127 letters, digits and hyphens; an optional version of 32 lower-case hexadecimal digits.<br>Maximum length: 2048<br>Pattern: `^https://[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,22}[a-z0-9]\.vault\.azure\.net/keys/[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,127}(/[0-9a-f]{32})?$`<br>Rule: the vault name must not contain consecutive hyphens (`!self.matches('^https://[a-z0-9-]*--')`) |

### GitBranch

GitBranch is a branch name. Names that git or a shell could read as something else (a leading dash,
refs/, HEAD, '..', '.lock') are refused, and so is the shadewright/ prefix Shadewright uses for its own
branches.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 255
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*$`

Validation rules:

- must be a plain branch name, not HEAD, refs/..., shadewright/... or one containing '..' or '.lock': `!self.contains('..') && !self.endsWith('.lock') && !self.contains('.lock/') && self != 'HEAD' && !self.startsWith('refs/') && !self.startsWith('shadewright/')`

Used by: [GitRepository](#gitrepository), [ResolvedSource](#resolvedsource).

### GitDirPath

GitDirPath is a directory relative to a repository root, "." for the root itself. Every segment follows
the rule of GitFilePath, so absolute paths, parent references, hidden directories and option-like names
are refused.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 512
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*)$`

Used by: [ResolvedSource](#resolvedsource).

### GitFilePath

GitFilePath is one YAML file, relative to a repository root. Every segment starts with a letter, digit or
underscore, so absolute paths, parent references, hidden directories such as .github, option-like names
and wildcards are all refused.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 512
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*\.ya?ml$`

Used by: [ResolvedSource](#resolvedsource).

### GitPathPattern

GitPathPattern is a glob, relative to a repository root, for files a policy may patch. `*` matches within one
path segment and `**` across segments; neither matches a segment that starts with a dot. The first segment
must be literal, so a pattern cannot cover the whole repository, and no segment may start with a dot or a
dash.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 512
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_*][A-Za-z0-9_.*-]*)*$`

Validation rules:

- must not contain '..': `!self.contains('..')`

Used by: [PolicyGitOps](#policygitops).

### GitRepository

GitRepository is a repository Shadewright may open pull requests in. Requests and policies refer to it by
name, so the model never chooses a URL or credentials.


Validation rules:

- github must be set if and only if provider is GitHub: `self.provider == 'GitHub' ? has(self.github) : !has(self.github)`
- a GitHub repository URL must be https://github.com/&lt;owner>/&lt;repo> in lower case, without .git: `self.provider != 'GitHub' || (self.url.matches('^https://github[.]com/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,38}/[a-z0-9_.-]{1,100}$') && !self.url.endsWith('.git') && !self.url.endsWith('/.') && !self.url.endsWith('/..'))`
- a GitHub target branch must start with a letter or digit, have at most 200 characters and not end with '.': `self.provider != 'GitHub' || (self.targetBranch.matches('^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,199}$') && !self.targetBranch.endsWith('.'))`

Used by: [RemediationSettingsSpec](#remediationsettingsspec).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [Name](#name) | Yes | name is how policies and requests refer to the repository.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `url` | string | Yes | url is the HTTPS clone URL, without credentials, query or fragment, and without a path segment that is '.' or '..'. It must match the URL of the Flux source that delivers a target, or no change is made. For GitHub it is https://github.com/&lt;owner>/&lt;repo> in lower case, without .git: an owner of 1 to 39 letters, digits and hyphens that starts with a letter or digit, and a repository name of 1 to 100 letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' other than '.' and '..' (it may start with '.', as in .github).<br>Maximum length: 512<br>Pattern: <code>^https://[a-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?(/(\.?[A-Za-z0-9_~-][A-Za-z0-9_.~-]*&#124;\.\.[A-Za-z0-9_.~-]+))+$</code> |
| `targetBranch` | [GitBranch](#gitbranch) | No | targetBranch is the only branch pull requests may target. The branch Flux tracks must equal it. For GitHub it starts with a letter or digit, has at most 200 characters and does not end with '.'.<br>Default: `main`<br>Maximum length: 255<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*$`<br>Rule: must be a plain branch name, not HEAD, refs/..., shadewright/... or one containing '..' or '.lock' |
| `provider` | [GitProviderType](#gitprovidertype) | Yes | provider selects the Git hosting adapter.<br>One of `GitHub` |
| `github` | [GitHubRepository](#githubrepository) | No | github holds GitHub App settings. |

### IncidentPhase

IncidentPhase summarizes an incident.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `Open`, `Analyzing`, `Proposed`, `Escalated`, `Resolved`

Used by: [IncidentStatus](#incidentstatus).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Open` | IncidentOpen means symptoms are being collected and no analysis is running. |
| `Analyzing` | IncidentAnalyzing means the analyzer is working on the incident. |
| `Proposed` | IncidentProposed means the analysis produced a RemediationRequest. |
| `Escalated` | IncidentEscalated means the analysis made no proposal and handed the incident to a human. |
| `Resolved` | IncidentResolved means the symptoms stopped or a remediation succeeded. |

### IntegrationStatus

IntegrationStatus reports one integration module that is enabled, detected or both. It is a report only:
the analyzer never reads it back to decide which integrations are active, it decides again from
spec.modules and live detection each time.


Validation rules:

- version is set if and only if the integration is detected: `self.detected == has(self.version)`
- an integration that is not detected is not active: `!self.active || self.detected`

Used by: [RemediationSettingsStatus](#remediationsettingsstatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [ModuleName](#modulename) | Yes | name is the integration module.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `detected` | boolean | Yes | detected is true when the cluster serves one of the group versions the module declares. An enabled name that no compiled-in module has is never detected. |
| `version` | string | No | version is the group version that detected the add-on, in discovery form (keda.sh/v1alpha1). Set if and only if the add-on is detected.<br>Maximum length: 253<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: <code>^([a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*/)?v[0-9]+((alpha&#124;beta)[0-9]+)?$</code> |
| `active` | boolean | Yes | active is true when the module contributes hooks: it is enabled in spec.modules.integrations and detected. It reports that decision and never feeds it. |

| `max` | integer | Yes | max is the highest maxReplicaCount the policy allows.<br>Maximum: 1000<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `maxIncreasePercent` | integer | No | maxIncreasePercent limits one increase relative to the previous value.<br>Default: `50`<br>Maximum: 1000<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `maxDecreasePercent` | integer | No | maxDecreasePercent limits one decrease relative to the previous value; 0 refuses every decrease.<br>Default: `0`<br>Maximum: 90<br>Minimum: 0 |

### MemoryLimitBounds

MemoryLimitBounds bounds SetContainerMemoryLimit. Decreases are refused unless maxDecreasePercent is set.


Validation rules:

- min and max must be whole bytes: `quantity(string(self.min)).isInteger() && quantity(string(self.max)).isInteger()`
- min must be at least 1Mi: `quantity(string(self.min)).compareTo(quantity('1Mi')) >= 0`
- max must be at most 1Ti: `quantity(string(self.max)).compareTo(quantity('1Ti')) <= 0`
- min must not be greater than max: `quantity(string(self.min)).compareTo(quantity(string(self.max))) <= 0`

Used by: [PolicyAction](#policyaction).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `min` | [Quantity](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#quantity-resource-core) | Yes | min is the lowest memory limit the policy allows. |
| `max` | [Quantity](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#quantity-resource-core) | Yes | max is the highest memory limit the policy allows. |
| `maxIncreasePercent` | integer | No | maxIncreasePercent limits one increase relative to the previous value.<br>Default: `50`<br>Maximum: 1000<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `maxDecreasePercent` | integer | No | maxDecreasePercent limits one decrease relative to the previous value; 0 refuses every decrease.<br>Default: `0`<br>Maximum: 90<br>Minimum: 0 |

### ModuleName

ModuleName names a cluster platform or integration module (design 2.4 and 2.5): a DNS label that starts with
a letter, at most 63 characters, the rule internal/modules checks when it builds its registry (a test keeps
the two equal). It is a pattern, not a list of known names, so a module compiled into a later release, or
shipped as a pack (ADR-0019), needs no schema change. A name that no compiled-in module has is accepted and
contributes nothing.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 63
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`

Used by: [IntegrationStatus](#integrationstatus), [Modules](#modules), [PlatformStatus](#platformstatus).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `generic` |  |

### Modules

Modules says which platform and integration modules the cluster admin enables (ADR-0018). Platform and
integration names are separate namespaces, so they are enabled in separate lists. A module contributes hooks
(symptom sources, diagnosis rules, tools, actions) only when it is enabled here and the analyzer detects it:
detection only reports and narrows, it never enables a module, and a module that is enabled but not
detected contributes nothing. Which modules are active is always worked out again from these lists and live
detection, never read back from status, which is only a report.


Used by: [RemediationSettingsSpec](#remediationsettingsspec).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platforms` | [ModuleName](#modulename) array | No | platforms are the platform modules enabled besides generic, which is always on and is not listed. More than one may be listed, so one settings file can serve clusters on different platforms: only the one the analyzer detects is active. Empty means generic only. The cap of 8 is also the most platform modules besides generic one binary may compile in (internal/modules refuses more), so every one of them can be enabled.<br>Maximum items: 8<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`<br>List type: set<br>Rule: the generic platform is always on and is not listed (`!('generic' in self)`) |
| `integrations` | [ModuleName](#modulename) array | No | integrations are the integration modules enabled. Each is active only while the analyzer detects its add-on. Empty means none. The cap of 32 is also the most integration modules one binary may compile in (internal/modules refuses more), so every one of them can be enabled.<br>Maximum items: 32<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`<br>List type: set |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiVersion` | string | Yes | apiVersion of the object, for example apps/v1 or keda.sh/v1alpha1.<br>Maximum length: 253<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: <code>^([a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*/)?v[0-9]+((alpha&#124;beta)[0-9]+)?$</code> |
| `kind` | string | Yes | kind of the object.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$` |
| `namespace` | string | No | namespace of the object; empty for cluster-scoped objects.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `name` | string | Yes | name of the object.<br>Maximum length: 253<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$` |
| `uid` | [UID](#uid) | No | uid of the object.<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |

### OccurrenceRecord

OccurrenceRecord is what an Incident counted of one occurrence (design 3.2). It holds no event text.


Used by: [IncidentStatus](#incidentstatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Yes | id names the occurrence: "event:" and the Event UID, or "termination:" and a hash of the pod UID, the container and the termination.<br>Maximum length: 76<br>Pattern: <code>^(event&#124;termination):[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,64}$</code> |
| `total` | integer | Yes | total is the highest total of the occurrence counted: the event's series count, or 1 for a termination.<br>Maximum: 2.147483647e+09<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `began` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | began is when the occurrence began: the event's creation time or the termination's finish time. Absent when the cluster did not report one. |

### PlanRepository

PlanRepository identifies the repository a plan was made for: the URL and provider installation taken from
RemediationSettings when planDigest was fixed. Cleanup of a superseded plan touches only this repository, so a
settings entry that now points elsewhere can never get an unrelated pull request closed.


Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | Yes | url is the repository URL from RemediationSettings.<br>Maximum length: 512 |
| `installationID` | integer | No | installationID is the provider installation that covers the repository; 0 when the provider has none.<br>Minimum: 0 |

### PlatformStatus

PlatformStatus reports which platform the analyzer detected and which one it uses. They differ when the
detected platform is not enabled in spec.modules.platforms: the analyzer then falls back to generic. So the
three cases are: nothing detected (detected left out, active generic), detected and enabled (active equal to
detected), and detected but not enabled (active generic). It is a report only: the analyzer never reads it
back to decide which platform to use, it decides again from spec.modules and live detection each time.


Validation rules:

- detected is left out, not generic, when no platform claims the cluster: `!has(self.detected) || self.detected != 'generic'`
- active is generic or the detected platform: `self.active == 'generic' || (has(self.detected) && self.active == self.detected)`

Used by: [RemediationSettingsStatus](#remediationsettingsstatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `detected` | [ModuleName](#modulename) | No | detected is the platform that claims every node with certainty. Left out when none does.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `active` | [ModuleName](#modulename) | Yes | active is the platform whose module contributes hooks: detected when it is enabled in spec.modules.platforms, generic otherwise.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$` |

### PolicyAction

PolicyAction allows one action type within bounds. Exactly the bounds member named by type is set.


Validation rules:

- adjustKedaMaxReplicas must be set if and only if type is AdjustKedaMaxReplicas: `self.type == 'AdjustKedaMaxReplicas' ? has(self.adjustKedaMaxReplicas) : !has(self.adjustKedaMaxReplicas)`
- setContainerMemoryLimit must be set if and only if type is SetContainerMemoryLimit: `self.type == 'SetContainerMemoryLimit' ? has(self.setContainerMemoryLimit) : !has(self.setContainerMemoryLimit)`

Used by: [RemediationPolicySpec](#remediationpolicyspec).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | [ActionType](#actiontype) | Yes | type is the allowed action.<br>One of `AdjustKedaMaxReplicas`, `SetContainerMemoryLimit` |
| `adjustKedaMaxReplicas` | [KedaMaxReplicasBounds](#kedamaxreplicasbounds) | No | adjustKedaMaxReplicas bounds AdjustKedaMaxReplicas.<br>Rule: min must not be greater than max |
| `setContainerMemoryLimit` | [MemoryLimitBounds](#memorylimitbounds) | No | setContainerMemoryLimit bounds SetContainerMemoryLimit.<br>Rule: min and max must be whole bytes<br>Rule: min must be at least 1Mi<br>Rule: max must be at most 1Ti<br>Rule: min must not be greater than max |

| `allowedPaths` | [GitPathPattern](#gitpathpattern) array | Yes | allowedPaths are glob patterns of files the policy may patch. The resolved file must match one.<br>Maximum items: 32<br>Maximum length: 512<br>Minimum items: 1<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_*][A-Za-z0-9_.*-]*)*$`<br>List type: set<br>Rule: must not contain '..' |

PolicyTargets says which objects a policy covers.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `url` | string | Yes | url of the pull request.<br>Maximum length: 2048<br>Pattern: `^https://` |
| `headSHA` | string | Yes | headSHA is the commit Shadewright pushed. Any other head stops automation.<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `renderedTargetHead` | string | No | renderedTargetHead is the head of the target branch at which the change in the pull request was last rendered and found to be exactly the planned one. While the pull request waits, the change is rendered again only when the target branch head is another commit; empty means not rendered since it was recorded.<br>Maximum length: 40<br>Minimum length: 40<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |

RecordID identifies an analysis record in the analysis store.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 256
- Minimum length: 1

### RemediationMode

RemediationMode says how a plan is carried out. GitOps is the only mode (ADR-0003).

- Underlying type: string
- One of `GitOps`

Used by: [RemediationRequestSpec](#remediationrequestspec).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `GitOps` | RemediationModeGitOps changes the cluster only through a pull request to the GitOps repository. |

### RemediationPhase

RemediationPhase summarizes where a request is. Conditions carry the reasons.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `Pending`, `PolicyChecked`, `PRCreated`, `AwaitingApproval`, `AutoMergeQueued`, `Merged`, `WaitingForDelivery`, `Verifying`, `Succeeded`, `Denied`, `Failed`, `Expired`, `Cancelled`, `Superseded`, `NeedsIntervention`

Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Pending` | PhasePending means the request was accepted and is waiting for the policy check. |
| `PolicyChecked` | PhasePolicyChecked means the policy allows the plan and the source in Git is resolved. |
| `PRCreated` | PhasePRCreated means the branch and pull request exist. |
| `AwaitingApproval` | PhaseAwaitingApproval means the pull request waits for human review. |
| `AutoMergeQueued` | PhaseAutoMergeQueued means policy allowed automation and auto-merge is enabled on the pull request. |
| `Merged` | PhaseMerged means the pull request is merged. |
| `WaitingForDelivery` | PhaseWaitingForDelivery means the change is merged and the GitOps controller has not applied it yet. |
| `Verifying` | PhaseVerifying means the change is delivered and the verification checks are running. |
| `Succeeded` | PhaseSucceeded means every verification check held for stableFor. Terminal. |
| `Denied` | PhaseDenied means policy refused the plan; no pull request is opened. Terminal. |
| `Failed` | PhaseFailed means a step failed, for example verification did not pass before the timeout. Terminal. |
| `Expired` | PhaseExpired means a step reached its deadline. Terminal. |
| `Cancelled` | PhaseCancelled means the request was cancelled before the change was merged. Terminal. |
| `Superseded` | PhaseSuperseded means an input of the plan digest changed, so the pull request is closed and a new request is needed. Terminal. |
| `NeedsIntervention` | PhaseNeedsIntervention means the controller cannot continue on its own, for example because the target is not declared in a plain manifest; a human must act. |

### RemediationPolicySpec

RemediationPolicySpec is what a policy allows: which namespaces may use it, which targets it covers, which
actions within which bounds, where in Git changes may go, and whether a human must approve. It is owned by
the cluster admin (ADR-0011).


Used by: [RemediationPolicy](#remediationpolicy).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requestNamespaces` | [Name](#name) array | No | requestNamespaces are the namespaces whose RemediationRequests may use this policy. A request from any other namespace is Denied, so being able to create requests somewhere does not grant this policy.<br>Default: `[shadewright-system]`<br>Maximum items: 16<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum items: 1<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$`<br>List type: set |
| `targets` | [PolicyTargets](#policytargets) | Yes | targets the policy covers. |
| `actions` | [PolicyAction](#policyaction) array | Yes | actions the policy allows, at most one entry per type. MaxItems follows the size of the action catalog; keeping it small keeps the CEL cost of the bounds rules within the API server's budget.<br>Maximum items: 4<br>Minimum items: 1<br>List type: map<br>List key: `type`<br>Rule: adjustKedaMaxReplicas must be set if and only if type is AdjustKedaMaxReplicas<br>Rule: setContainerMemoryLimit must be set if and only if type is SetContainerMemoryLimit |
| `gitOps` | [PolicyGitOps](#policygitops) | Yes | gitOps limits where changes may be made. |
| `approval` | [ApprovalMode](#approvalmode) | No | approval says whether human review is always required.<br>Default: `Required`<br>One of `Required`, `Optional` |

### RemediationPolicyStatus

RemediationPolicyStatus reports whether the policy is usable.


Used by: [RemediationPolicy](#remediationpolicy).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | No | observedGeneration is the generation the status describes. |
| `conditions` | [Condition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#condition-v1-meta) array | No | conditions report problems such as an unknown repositoryRef.<br>List type: map<br>List key: `type` |

### RemediationRequestSpec

RemediationRequestSpec is one concrete plan. It is immutable: a different plan is a new request, so an
approval can never carry over to a changed plan. It names what to change, not where: the repository, branch
and file are resolved by the controller (ADR-0012), so the author cannot point a change at another file.
Each action type fixes the kinds it may target.


Validation rules:

- spec is immutable; a changed plan is a new RemediationRequest: `self == oldSelf`
- AdjustKedaMaxReplicas can only target a keda.sh ScaledObject: `self.action.type != 'AdjustKedaMaxReplicas' || (self.targetRef.apiVersion.startsWith('keda.sh/') && self.targetRef.kind == 'ScaledObject')`
- SetContainerMemoryLimit can only target an apps/v1 Deployment or StatefulSet: `self.action.type != 'SetContainerMemoryLimit' || (self.targetRef.apiVersion == 'apps/v1' && self.targetRef.kind in ['Deployment', 'StatefulSet'])`

Used by: [RemediationRequest](#remediationrequest).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `incidentRef` | [IncidentRef](#incidentref) | Yes | incidentRef is the incident this plan answers. |
| `targetRef` | [ObjectRef](#objectref) | Yes | targetRef is the live object the change is about.<br>Rule: targetRef.uid is required (`has(self.uid) && size(self.uid) > 0`)<br>Rule: targetRef.namespace is required (`has(self.namespace) && size(self.namespace) > 0`) |
| `mode` | [RemediationMode](#remediationmode) | No | mode is how the plan is carried out.<br>Default: `GitOps`<br>One of `GitOps` |
| `approvalRequired` | boolean | No | approvalRequired asks for human review. false is a request for automation that policy may refuse; it never lowers policy or repository rules.<br>Default: `true` |
| `policyRef` | [Name](#name) | Yes | policyRef names the RemediationPolicy that must allow this plan.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `action` | [Action](#action) | Yes | action is the typed change.<br>Rule: adjustKedaMaxReplicas must be set if and only if type is AdjustKedaMaxReplicas<br>Rule: setContainerMemoryLimit must be set if and only if type is SetContainerMemoryLimit |
| `verification` | [Verification](#verification) | No | verification says when the change counts as a success.<br>Default: `{}`<br>Rule: stableFor must be at least 1m<br>Rule: timeout must be at most 24h<br>Rule: timeout must be longer than stableFor |

### RemediationRequestStatus

RemediationRequestStatus is written only by the remediation controller.


Used by: [RemediationRequest](#remediationrequest).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | No | observedGeneration is the generation the status describes. |
| `phase` | [RemediationPhase](#remediationphase) | No | phase summarizes progress.<br>One of `Pending`, `PolicyChecked`, `PRCreated`, `AwaitingApproval`, `AutoMergeQueued`, `Merged`, `WaitingForDelivery`, `Verifying`, `Succeeded`, `Denied`, `Failed`, `Expired`, `Cancelled`, `Superseded`, `NeedsIntervention` |
| `effectiveApprovalRequired` | boolean | No | effectiveApprovalRequired is what policy decided, which may be stricter than spec.approvalRequired. |
| `source` | [ResolvedSource](#resolvedsource) | No | source is where the change is made, resolved by the controller before the policy check. |
| `planDigest` | string | No | planDigest covers the semantic change, the target UID, the resolved source with the repository URL and provider installation from RemediationSettings, and the policy UID and generation. It is fixed when the branch is created; if any input changes later, the request becomes Superseded and its PR is closed.<br>Pattern: `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `planRepository` | [PlanRepository](#planrepository) | No | planRepository is the repository and installation the plan digest covers, set together with planDigest. |
| `policyRevision` | string | No | policyRevision is the policy name and generation the decision used, as name/generation. The policy UID is recorded next to it, because a deleted and recreated policy can reach the same generation again.<br>Maximum length: 128 |
| `policyUID` | [UID](#uid) | No | policyUID is the UID of the policy the decision used. It is part of the plan digest.<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |
| `pullRequest` | [PullRequestStatus](#pullrequeststatus) | No | pullRequest is set once the pull request exists. |
| `deadline` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | deadline is when the current step gives up. |
| `conditions` | [Condition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#condition-v1-meta) array | No | conditions explain the phase. Types: PolicyAllowed, PullRequestOpened, Approved, Delivered, Verified and PlanFresh.<br>List type: map<br>List key: `type` |

### RemediationSettingsSpec

RemediationSettingsSpec holds cluster-wide settings, including the kill switch.


Used by: [RemediationSettings](#remediationsettings).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paused` | boolean | No | paused stops every write: pull requests, auto-merge and issues. Analysis continues. Checked right before each write.<br>Default: `false` |
| `maxConcurrentRemediations` | integer | No | maxConcurrentRemediations limits requests between PolicyChecked and a terminal phase.<br>Default: `1`<br>Maximum: 20<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `maxAnalysesPerDay` | integer | No | maxAnalysesPerDay limits model-backed analyses per UTC day; 0 disables the model.<br>Default: `100`<br>Maximum: 10000<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `repositories` | [GitRepository](#gitrepository) array | No | repositories Shadewright may open pull requests in. URLs are unique, so a Flux source matches at most one entry.<br>Maximum items: 16<br>List type: map<br>List key: `name`<br>Rule: repository URLs must be unique (`self.all(r, self.exists_one(s, s.url == r.url))`) |
| `modules` | [Modules](#modules) | No | modules enables platform and integration modules. Left out, only the generic platform is on and no integration is: nothing is enabled because it was detected. |

### RemediationSettingsStatus

RemediationSettingsStatus reports whether the settings are usable.


Used by: [RemediationSettings](#remediationsettings).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | No | observedGeneration is the generation the status describes. |
| `conditions` | [Condition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#condition-v1-meta) array | No | conditions report problems. The analyzer writes UnknownModules: True when spec.modules names a module that it does not have compiled in, which then contributes nothing; and DetectionFailed: True when its last run could not list the nodes or read the discovery API, so the report is from the last run that succeeded, or shows only generic active when none has.<br>List type: map<br>List key: `type` |
| `platform` | [PlatformStatus](#platformstatus) | No | platform is the platform the analyzer detected and the one it uses. The analyzer writes it at start, when spec changes and every 10 minutes (ADR-0024), with the only write it has outside the operator namespace. Status is a report, never an input: no component reads any field of it to decide anything.<br>Rule: detected is left out, not generic, when no platform claims the cluster<br>Rule: active is generic or the detected platform |
| `integrations` | [IntegrationStatus](#integrationstatus) array | No | integrations lists every integration module that is enabled or detected, with whether it is active. A detected add-on whose module is not enabled is listed too, so the cluster admin sees what could be enabled. Written like platform. At most 64: 32 enabled (the spec cap) and 32 more detected, since a detected add-on needs a compiled-in module and internal/modules refuses more than 32.<br>Maximum items: 64<br>List type: map<br>List key: `name`<br>Rule: version is set if and only if the integration is detected<br>Rule: an integration that is not detected is not active |

### ResolvedSource

ResolvedSource is where the controller found the target's declaration in Git (ADR-0012). It is derived from
the Flux objects that deliver the target and from RemediationSettings, never taken from the request.


Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repositoryRef` | [Name](#name) | Yes | repositoryRef is the RemediationSettings entry whose URL matches the Flux source.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `targetBranch` | [GitBranch](#gitbranch) | Yes | targetBranch is the branch the pull request targets: the branch Flux tracks, which must equal the repository's targetBranch in RemediationSettings.<br>Maximum length: 255<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*$`<br>Rule: must be a plain branch name, not HEAD, refs/..., shadewright/... or one containing '..' or '.lock' |
| `path` | [GitFilePath](#gitfilepath) | Yes | path is the file that declares the target.<br>Maximum length: 512<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*\.ya?ml$` |
| `buildPath` | [GitDirPath](#gitdirpath) | No | buildPath is the directory the Flux Kustomization builds (its spec.path, "." for the repository root). Before every commit the pull request step renders it with and without the change and refuses anything but the planned difference (design 8.2, steps 4 and 5). The policy check always sets it, and the plan digest covers it; a request without it is never committed.<br>Maximum length: 512<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: <code>^(\.&#124;[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*)$</code> |
| `baseCommit` | string | Yes | baseCommit is the full SHA of the target branch the change was made against. It is fixed when the branch is created; later merges to the target branch do not change it.<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |

### SetContainerMemoryLimit

SetContainerMemoryLimit changes resources.limits.memory of one container. previous must match the file in
Git when the patch is applied, or the plan is stale. Both values are whole bytes between 1Mi and 1Ti.


Validation rules:

- desired must differ from previous: `quantity(string(self.desired)).compareTo(quantity(string(self.previous))) != 0`
- previous and desired must be whole bytes: `quantity(string(self.previous)).isInteger() && quantity(string(self.desired)).isInteger()`
- previous must be between 1Mi and 1Ti: `quantity(string(self.previous)).compareTo(quantity('1Mi')) >= 0 && quantity(string(self.previous)).compareTo(quantity('1Ti')) <= 0`
- desired must be between 1Mi and 1Ti: `quantity(string(self.desired)).compareTo(quantity('1Mi')) >= 0 && quantity(string(self.desired)).compareTo(quantity('1Ti')) <= 0`

Used by: [Action](#action).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | string | Yes | container is the container name in the pod template.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `previous` | [Quantity](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#quantity-resource-core) | Yes | previous is the limit the plan was made against. |
| `desired` | [Quantity](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#quantity-resource-core) | Yes | desired is the new limit. |

Signer says where the GitHub App private key lives. The key never enters the cluster.


Validation rules:

- a signer must be configured: `has(self.azureKeyVault)`

Used by: [GitHubRepository](#githubrepository).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `azureKeyVault` | [AzureKeyVaultKey](#azurekeyvaultkey) | No | azureKeyVault signs with a non-exportable Key Vault key through workload identity. |

### UID

UID is a Kubernetes object UID in its canonical lower-case form.

- Underlying type: string
- Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`

Used by: [IncidentRef](#incidentref), [ObjectRef](#objectref), [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

### Verification

Verification says when a delivered change counts as a success. The controller always adds the checks the
action type needs (DeliveryRevisionApplied, plus KedaReady or NoNewOOMKills), so a request can only make
verification stricter.


Validation rules:

- stableFor must be at least 1m: `!has(self.stableFor) || duration(self.stableFor) >= duration('1m')`
- timeout must be at most 24h: `!has(self.timeout) || duration(self.timeout) <= duration('24h')`
- timeout must be longer than stableFor: `!has(self.timeout) || !has(self.stableFor) || duration(self.timeout) > duration(self.stableFor)`

Used by: [RemediationRequestSpec](#remediationrequestspec).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout` | [Duration](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1#Duration) | No | timeout is how long to wait for delivery and stability before giving up.<br>Default: `10m` |
| `stableFor` | [Duration](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1#Duration) | No | stableFor is how long all checks must hold.<br>Default: `3m` |
| `checks` | [VerificationCheck](#verificationcheck) array | No | checks to run in addition to the ones the action type always needs.<br>One of `DeliveryRevisionApplied`, `WorkloadHealthy`, `KedaReady`, `QueueBacklogDecreasing`, `NoNewOOMKills`<br>Maximum items: 8<br>List type: set |

### VerificationCheck

VerificationCheck is a named, deterministic check run after delivery. DeliveryRevisionApplied: the GitOps
controller has applied the revision that contains the merged change. WorkloadHealthy: the target workload
is available and its rollout is complete. KedaReady: the KEDA ScaledObject reports Ready.
QueueBacklogDecreasing: the backlog that drives the ScaledObject is going down. NoNewOOMKills: no container
of the target is OOMKilled after the change.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `DeliveryRevisionApplied`, `WorkloadHealthy`, `KedaReady`, `QueueBacklogDecreasing`, `NoNewOOMKills`

Used by: [Verification](#verification).
